openFindings.finding: The broad warm amber color and thin luminous border are substantially improved, but most driving views still read as opaque ochre/brown panels with faint wavy markings. There is little convincing layer separation, enclosed inclusions or warm reflected depth compared with the selected hollow-tree scene concept. Removing glare has flattened much of the surface.
openFindings.fix: Retain the present amber palette/border and readable lanes; introduce several scales/depths of internal resin structure and restrained view-dependent warm reflection/refraction/roughness response. The target is perceived deep resin at driving scale, not a demand for a costly physically exact transmission pipeline. Keep bright highlights bounded and preserve sap/resin contrast.

openFindings.finding: The whole hollow is preserved and bark texture is better, but nearby bark still resolves into largely vertical bands and long flat faces. Ordinary crown silhouettes look like repeated coarse leaf cutouts, while Mycelium fans appear as very regular cyan umbrella stacks. Add localized medium-scale bark/root/branch variation and motivated shading; give leaf/fungal families varied volume, spacing, underside/gill color and softened material response so repetition is less obvious. Prefer a small number of better modules/materials over dense added detail.
